title: SpeechNexusPublicErrors
description: Single source of truth for the OpenAI-compatible public error envelope shared by the speech, realtime, admin, and workbench public protocols. Internal control-plane errors add their own diagnostic fields instead of reusing this envelope.

retryable.description: Whether the same request can succeed without an out-of-band change. The value belongs to the refusing operation's disposition, not to the status or the code: one operation's 409 may ask the caller to wait out a cleanup (retryable) while another 409 in the same operation reports a spent idempotency key (not retryable), so a caller reads this field instead of inferring retryability from the status. `true` means repeating the same request later can be admitted with no operator, configuration or data change: a released capacity lease, a concurrent writer finishing, a connection-level outcome that the original identity replays, and a cleanup that completes on its own all qualify. `false` means the same request is answered the same way until something outside the request changes, and the operation's published code and message name that change: provisioning the workspace quota, re-signing an engine readiness receipt, restoring a disabled instance, or re-registering against an approved recipe. The field never grants permission to drop an identity: a replayed unknown outcome is recovered under its original Idempotency-Key because the outcome is unknown, not because a value permits it, and every operation states that requirement in its own 5xx vocabulary. The meaning is per operation rather than global, so an operation that publishes a per-code value states it in its own contract (`contracts/workbench-openapi.yaml` for the workbench operations) instead of restating this field.

OperationRecovery.description: Query GET /v1/nexus/operations/{operation_id}. This identity is the original execution; retrying never creates a second execution.
